How it works

From first step to fully set up, in four moves.

A guided journey, not a single transaction. Here is how it comes together and how you stay in control once it is live.

  1. 01

    Know your eligibility

    We assess your portfolio and history against clear criteria, then assign an approved limit based on the value and classification of your holdings and your overall profile.

    • Portfolio and history reviewed against defined criteria
    • Limit set by the value and quality of your collateral
    • A suitability assessment that confirms it is right for you
  2. 02

    Set up your account

    Once approved, a dedicated account is created and linked to your existing profile, with your eligible assets and balances recognised automatically.

    • A dedicated account, linked to your existing profile
    • Eligible assets and cash recognised automatically
    • No separate paperwork to arrange
  3. 03

    Put it to work

    Use your new capacity across the approved universe. Everything updates automatically as prices and values change, so your position is always current.

    • Act across the full approved list
    • Values recalculated in real time
    • Build or diversify without unwinding what you hold
  4. 04

    Stay in control

    Real-time tools show your utilisation, coverage and headroom, so there are no surprises. Clear triggers and transparent communication keep you ahead of every move.

    • Live view of utilisation, coverage and headroom
    • Defined triggers and transparent communication
    • Clear actions whenever conditions change
Talk to our team
How it works

From sign up to reconciled reporting, in five steps.

One agreement, one channel, then day-to-day messaging that stays standardised.

  1. 1

    Sign up

    Agree a product service agreement with Emirates NBD through your Relationship Manager.

  2. 2

    Connect via SCORE

    Join the SWIFT closed user group that links corporates to banks.

  3. 3

    Send instructions

    Push single MT messages over SWIFT FIN, or files and batches over SWIFT FileACT.

  4. 4

    Receive and reconcile

    Pull statements and reporting from multiple banks through the one channel.

  5. 5

    Track status

    Get network ACK or NACK on FIN messages, and response messages such as pain.002 on FileACT.

Markets · Emirates NBD Research

OPEC+ sticks with incremental increases in output

EB
Edward Bell Acting Group Head of Research and Chief Economist
20 November 2025 2 min read

A steady hand on output buys OPEC+ time, but the outlook for oil market balances still points to a substantial inventory build.

Targets held steady into Q1 2026

For the first time this year OPEC+ set out production targets for longer than a month ahead, agreeing to increase production by 137k b/d for December and then hold targets at those levels until the end of Q1 2026.

Our history

Four decades shaping
banking in the region.

From a single Dubai bank to a global group serving over fourteen million customers worldwide.

1997

Emirates Bank International founded

Emirates Bank International was established in Dubai, laying the foundation for what would become one of the region's most trusted banking institutions.

2007

Historic merger creates Emirates NBD

Emirates Bank International and National Bank of Dubai merged to form Emirates NBD, creating the UAE's largest bank by assets and a regional powerhouse.

2013

Launch of businessONLINE

Emirates NBD launched businessONLINE, its flagship corporate digital banking platform, enabling businesses to manage payments and liquidity across 180+ countries.

2019

Acquisition of DenizBank

Emirates NBD completed the landmark acquisition of DenizBank in Turkey, significantly expanding its global presence and customer base to over 14 million.

2022

Digital banking leadership

Emirates NBD was recognised as the Most Innovative Bank in the Middle East, with over 90% of transactions conducted digitally across its platforms.

2024

AI-powered banking platform

Launched next-generation AI-driven financial tools including ENBD X and businessONLINE X, delivering personalised banking experiences for millions of customers.

2025

Simpler. Better. Smarter.

Emirates NBD continues to lead digital transformation with its ecosystem of tools — businessONLINE, smartTRADE, Emirates NBD Pay and smartSCF — serving corporate clients across 13 countries.

Atoms

Buttons

One button system: type, glyph, icon mode, size and corner radius. Types are named by role, never by colour — the paint comes from the brand tokens, and the glyph is a class, never markup.

Types — filled (primary), accent filled (secondary), outlined, text

Open an account Talk to an advisor View details Read the report

With a glyph — add the modifier, any type. Trailing by default

Open an account Talk to an advisor Download brochure Read the report

Leading glyph — the same modifier plus .is-ic-start

All case studies Search the site Annual report (PDF)

The vocabulary — 14 glyphs, named for what the control does

is-arrow is-arrow-back is-next is-back is-up is-down is-up-right is-close is-plus is-minus is-download is-search is-play is-pause

Directional glyphs (arrow, arrow-back, next, back, up-right) mirror automatically under dir="rtl"; the rest never do. In forced-colours mode every glyph repaints with the system button ink.

Icon only — .btn-icon, always a circle, the label stays for screen readers

Sizes — the glyph scales with the button (--ic-size: 14 / 16 / 17 / 18 / 20px)

Extra small Small Default Large Extra large

Corner radius — per-size default vs pill

Default Pill Default Pill

States & special

Close facility Explore capabilities

The disabled state comes from the attribute; outline-light is the explicit outline for dark surfaces — flip the Surface control to see it earn its place, and watch the glyph follow the ink.

Atoms

Card surfaces

One look class, one paint class, one finish — every card in the system. The finish modifiers carry no colour at all: surfaces own the fill and the ink, is-* owns the border and the shadow. An unpainted card-panel is a light island — put it on navy and its content keeps light-mode ink automatically.

Finish × paint are independent — the same three finishes (raised · tile · flat) over three surfaces

White · raised

Hairline border and the one canonical shadow. The everyday card.

card-panel surface-white

Grey · raised

Only the fill changed — the finish is untouched.

card-panel surface-grey

Navy · raised

The surface brings its own ink tokens — white on navy, on ANY section surface.

card-panel surface-primary

White · tile

is-tile removes the rule and the shadow. It adds no fill of its own.

card-panel surface-white is-tile

Grey · tile

The quiet tile for dense grids — the estate's most-used card.

card-panel surface-grey is-tile

Navy · tile

The same finish over a dark paint — impossible while is-tile still smuggled a grey fill.

card-panel surface-primary is-tile

White · flat

Border only, no shadow — for calm layouts where depth would be noise.

card-panel surface-white is-flat

Grey · flat

Keeps the hairline, drops the lift.

card-panel surface-grey is-flat

Navy · flat

Nine cells, two axes, no variants — that is the whole model.

card-panel surface-primary is-flat

The rest of the paint axis — a surface class on the SAME element (works on any bounded container, not just cards)

Grey 2

The deeper app grey. Still a light island. Replaces the retired is-grey fill modifier.

card-panel surface-grey-2 is-tile

Blue

Brand-blue frame; on-surface ink flips to light.

card-panel surface-accent

Clear (null surface)

No paint and no ink of its own — the section themes right through it. Flip Surface to Navy to watch it adapt.

card-panel surface-clear

Hover (link card)

The one interaction finish: adds the lift on hover, for cards that are one whole link.

Explore

Glass — one frosted family in four strengths (dark or image ground only: the ink stays white)

Glass

Translucent white, blurred, white ink. The frosted-panel-on-navy default.

card-panel surface-glass

Glass 25

Same recipe, a quarter-white fill. Strength is paint, so it is spelled as a surface.

card-panel surface-glass-25

Glass 50

Half-white glass fill.

card-panel surface-glass-50

Glass 75

Near-opaque. Reserve it for a busy photo ground and run /audit.html — white ink on a three-quarter white fill is tight.

card-panel surface-glass-75

The other look — card-media: the image IS the card (media-cover + an .ov scrim; ink is white by construction)

Media

Clipped, rounded, white ink.

card-media + .ov

Media — flat scrim

Same look, a different .ov tone and strength.

card-media + ov-scrim ov-50

Boxless — no look class at all

Content straight on the section is the model's null case, not an oversight: drop card-panel and card-media and the card is just its content. Cards — Plain, People, List and Testimonials ship that way.

cd-card  (nothing else)
Illustration

Illustration video

A looping illustration with its background baked into the file — no player chrome, no controls, no overlay. The bake carries the surface it will sit on, so the video reads as drawn straight onto the page rather than pasted over it.

Full-width panel · light — white bake, white face

The section band under it is grey and the frame is white — the only edge you can see is the frame’s own radius. Nothing in the markup knows what the animation is.

Full-width panel · navy — navy bake, navy face

One motion, two files. Putting the white bake here would paint a white rectangle over the navy — the failure this doctrine exists to prevent.

Inset in a grid · the illustration is a card slot

Payments that settle while you watch

Inset in a light card, the bake matches the card face — not the section. The face is what the video sits on, so the face is what gets baked.

illustration-signal-white.mp4

The same story on a dark card

The card carries its own paint and its own ink tokens; the illustration carries a bake made for that paint. Two assets, zero component code.

illustration-signal-navy.mp4
Illustration

Lottie

Vector illustration that arrives as a JSON asset and renders as live SVG — a few kilobytes, resolution-free, and transparent, so one file sits on any surface. Reach for it when the artwork is drawn; reach for the baked video when it is rendered.

One asset · every surface — the same JSON on a light and a dark face

Always on, always live

Drawn on transparency, so the card face shows through. Nothing about the asset changes between these two cards — only the surface under it.

assets/lottie/demo-pulse.json · 3 KB

The same file, no second export

Where a baked video needs one file per face, a transparent Lottie needs one file full stop. That is the trade: transparency and size against photographic richness.

assets/lottie/demo-pulse.json · 3 KB

The poster · the still, the sizer and the reduced-motion state

No motion, no download

Under a reduced-motion preference the recipe stops before the network: the player is never fetched, the JSON is never fetched, and this frame stays. Export it from frame 0 of the animation so the two never disagree.

Terms & Conditions

Updated schedule of charges

Effective 1 July 2025, the Schedule of Charges for Corporate & Institutional Banking products has been updated. Please review the changes below before continuing to use businessONLINE.

1. Wire transfer fees for international payments have been revised in line with prevailing correspondent banking rates. Domestic payment processing remains free of charge for all account tiers.

2. Trade finance tariffs for letters of credit and guarantees are now tiered by transaction value, with preferential pricing for high-volume clients.

3. FX conversion spreads remain unchanged. Real-time rates continue to be available through the businessONLINE markets module.

Terms & Conditions

Full schedule of charges

1. Wire transfer fees for international payments have been revised in line with prevailing correspondent banking rates. Domestic payment processing remains free of charge for all account tiers.

2. Trade finance tariffs for letters of credit and guarantees are now tiered by transaction value, with preferential pricing for high-volume clients.

3. FX conversion spreads remain unchanged. Real-time rates continue to be available through the businessONLINE markets module.

4. Account maintenance charges apply per account per calendar month and are debited on the first working day of the following month.

5. Cheque book issuance for corporate accounts is charged per book. Special cheque printing is quoted on request.

6. Payroll processing through the WPS channel is charged per employee record per cycle, with volume tiers applied quarterly.

7. Standing instructions are charged per execution. Failed executions due to insufficient funds incur a separate handling fee.

8. Duplicate statements and audit confirmation letters are produced within five working days of a complete request.

9. Escrow and agency service fees follow the schedule agreed in the relevant service agreement and are invoiced separately.

10. Collection items in foreign currency are subject to correspondent charges, which are passed through at cost.

11. Safe deposit and custody services are billed annually in advance, with pro-rata refunds on early termination.

12. Digital channel subscriptions cover platform access, token issuance and standard support during business hours.

13. Out-of-hours support and priority processing carry a surcharge, quoted at the time of request.

14. All charges are exclusive of VAT, which is applied at the prevailing rate under UAE law.
